report_md:
# Sector rotation — development report

**Verdict: fail (cost-fragile, narrow plateau).** The XLK/XLU leadership state
earns **37.65% CAGR / 48.79% max DD / 1.09 Sharpe** at 1 bp over 2016-2023.
That clears the published TQQQ CAGR bar (36.72%) by only 0.93 pp, cuts the
drawdown from 82.29% to 48.79%, and is strongly non-random (placebo 98th
percentile). But it fails at 5 bp (34.11%) and 10 bp (29.83%), and only two of
the eight pre-registered cells clear the 1 bp bar. The result is a genuine
risk-management signal, not a cost-robust above-TQQQ winner. 2024-2026 is
untouched.

## Development metrics

| Cost | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | Vol | Exposure | Fills | Turnover |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 bp | 37.65% | 48.79% | 1.09 | 1.58 | 35.1% | 100.0% | 519 | 2,210x |
| 5 bp | 34.11% | 51.58% | 1.01 | 1.47 | 35.1% | 100.0% | 519 | 1,913x |
| 10 bp | 29.83% | 54.86% | 0.92 | 1.33 | 35.1% | 100.0% | 519 | 1,603x |

There are **519 fills across 260 independent fill days** (about 65 fills and
33 events per year), comfortably above the 100-fill / 30-event floor. Average
weights are **45.8% QQQ, 29.0% TQQQ, 25.2% BIL**. The book is always fully
invested in one of those three assets.

The cost drag is large: 7.8 pp of CAGR from 1 bp to 10 bp. The 20-day leg
crosses its threshold often, and each state change trades the full book. This
is the family's central weakness.

## Subperiods and years

| Window | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 26.37% | 28.55% | 1.11 |
| 2020-2021 | 64.50% | 31.62% | 1.37 |
| 2022-2023 | 33.71% | 29.21% | 0.89 |

| Year | Return |
|---|---:|
| 2016 | +11.6% |
| 2017 | +25.6% |
| 2018 | +7.1% |
| 2019 | +61.0% |
| 2020 | +185.4% |
| 2021 | -4.0% |
| 2022 | -13.5% |
| 2023 | +104.1% |

All three subperiods are positive, so the subperiod kill does not fire. But
2021 and 2022 are negative years: the sector signal was early in 2021 and
whipsawed in 2022. The result is carried by 2020 (+185%) and 2023 (+104%).
Excluding 2023, the CAGR is **29.93%** with a 0.95 Sharpe, so the full-window
headline overstates the typical year.

## Plateau (8 pre-registered cells)

| Windows | TQQQ z | BIL z | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Fills | Turnover |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **20/60** | **+0.50** | **-0.50** | **37.65%** | **48.8%** | **1.09** | **519** | **2,210x** |
| 20/60 | +0.50 | -0.75 | 38.23% | 51.8% | 1.09 | 457 | 2,172x |
| 20/60 | +0.75 | -0.50 | 27.96% | 47.7% | 0.96 | 491 | 1,561x |
| 20/60 | +0.75 | -0.75 | 28.50% | 50.7% | 0.96 | 429 | 1,523x |
| 20 only | +0.50 | -0.50 | 30.18% | 60.5% | 0.94 | 753 | 3,109x |
| 20 only | +0.75 | -0.75 | 25.55% | 57.9% | 0.87 | 609 | 2,126x |
| 60 only | +0.50 | -0.50 | 20.89% | 69.3% | 0.72 | 495 | 1,348x |
| 60 only | +0.75 | -0.75 | 27.69% | 59.0% | 0.91 | 329 | 1,263x |

This is **not a plateau; it is a narrow ridge**. Only the two 20/60 cells with
`tqqq_z = 0.50` clear the 1 bp bar. Raising the TQQQ threshold to 0.75 costs
about 9-10 pp, and both single-horizon families fail. The 20-day leg carries
the timing information, but it is also the source of the turnover. The blend
is the only configuration that works, which is a real fragility.

## Placebo and static attribution

* **Circular-shift placebo (100 shifts):** median CAGR 16.9%, 95th percentile
  33.0%; the real 37.65% is above 98 of 100 shifts (percentile 0.98). Median
  placebo Sharpe 0.61 vs the real 1.09 (percentile 0.98). Median placebo max
  DD 62.4% vs the real 48.8%.
* **Static book at the average weights (45.8/29.0/25.2):** 22.40% CAGR / 47.6%
  DD / 0.84 Sharpe. The timing adds **15.25 pp** of CAGR and 0.25 Sharpe, so
  the state is not just a disguised fixed mix.

## Correlation to the nine current winners

| Winner | Correlation |
|---|---:|
| ratio-froth | 0.504 |
| vol-scaled-crash-stop | 0.619 |
| relative-value-tqqq | 0.641 |
| fomc-opex-window | 0.536 |
| family-session-timing | 0.526 |
| family-short-reversal | 0.543 |
| family-rebalance-flow | 0.644 |
| family-intraday-microstructure-day | 0.427 |
| family-ml-microstructure | 0.572 |

Range **0.43 to 0.64**. The highest are `family-rebalance-flow` (0.644) and
`relative-value-tqqq` (0.641); the lowest is
`family-intraday-microstructure-day` (0.427). No correlation approaches the
0.95 duplicate threshold. Daily-return correlation with the other two new
families is 0.37 (breadth) and 0.59 (crypto).

A same-map **QQQ 20/60 momentum** control (`±0.50`, TQQQ/BIL/QQQ) earns
18.55% CAGR / 63.7% DD / 0.72 Sharpe and correlates **0.735** with this
strategy. The sector signal adds 19.1 pp of CAGR, but the 0.735 correlation
says part of the edge is tech-beta timing rather than a pure sector effect.
That is a further reason not to call this a clean new winner.

## Kill criteria

| Criterion | Result | Pass? |
|---|---|---:|
| 1 bp CAGR > 36.72% | 37.65% | yes (marginal) |
| 1 bp max DD < 82.29% | 48.79% | yes |
| 10 bp CAGR > 36.72% | 29.83% | **no** |
| Placebo percentile >= 90% | 98% | yes |
| Max winner correlation <= 0.95 | 0.644 | yes |
| >= 100 fills / >= 30 events | 519 / 260 | yes |
| No negative subperiod | all positive | yes |
| Static blend not within 1 pp | 22.40% vs 37.65% | yes |
| Causality audit | 25/25 perturb, 25/25 mapping | yes |

The only failed kill is the 10 bp cost check. Because the 1 bp margin is also
under 1 pp and the plateau is a narrow ridge, the honest verdict is **fail**,
not "pass with caveats."

## Caveats

* **Cost fragility is structural.** The 20-day leg is the source of both the
  alpha and the turnover; slowing it to 60 days removes the alpha.
* **The plateau is narrow.** Only the 20/60 blend at `tqqq_z = 0.50` clears the
  1 bp bar. The result is not robust to a modestly stricter entry threshold.
* **Two negative years.** 2021 (-4.0%) and 2022 (-13.5%) show the signal can
  be early and can whipsaw. The 2020 and 2023 tails carry the headline.
* **2016 is partly a warm-up year.** The 60-day z-score needs 120 observations,
  so early 2016 is QQQ; +11.6% is not a full TQQQ year.
* **Partial QQQ-trend overlap.** The 0.735 correlation to a same-map QQQ
  momentum control is high, even though the CAGR difference is large.
* **Same-session ETF close.** XLK/XLU close at 16:00 ET, the same close used
  for the decision; the fill is the next session's open. This is a standard
  daily-close convention, not a same-bar fill.
* **Development only.** No 2024-2026 data was read. The result is a frozen
  development record, not a holdout claim.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd research/new/family-sector-rotation
python strategy.py        # rewrites result.json
```

`build_weights(ts, opens, closes)` returns `(n, 3)` minute weights and accepts
either the shared minute panel or a daily panel. The development guard rejects
panels extending past 2023-12-29 unless the caller supplies `end`.
hypothesis_md:
# family-sector-rotation — hypothesis and pre-registration

**Slug:** `family-sector-rotation`
**Family:** sector rotation (growth vs defensive leadership)
**Development window:** 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29 only. 2024-2026 is not
loaded or inspected by the development run.
**Benchmark bar:** TQQQ 36.72% CAGR / 82.29% max DD / 0.82 Sharpe (published
1-minute-mark bar). TQQQ on this panel is 36.15% / 82.29% / 0.80.

## 1. Mechanism

TQQQ is a constant 3x wrapper on QQQ, so its return is dominated by the
Nasdaq-100 trend. But the composition of that trend matters. When technology
(XLK) is leading utilities (XLU), the market is paying for growth and
duration; the risk appetite that supports a 3x Nasdaq position is broad and
persistent. When utilities are leading technology, investors are moving toward
defensive cash flows and rate-sensitive safety; that is a risk-off state in
which a 3x daily-reset wrapper is poorly compensated.

The primary object is therefore the **XLK/XLU relative return**, not a QQQ
price trend, a volatility estimate, or a calendar clock. The 20-day leg
captures an emerging rotation; the 60-day leg confirms that it is a regime
rather than a one-week sector squall. Both legs are z-scored against their own
trailing 252-session distributions so the two horizons are comparable.

The mapping is long-only:

* strong tech leadership (`score >= +0.50`) -> **TQQQ**;
* strong defensive leadership (`score <= -0.50`) -> **BIL**;
* otherwise -> **QQQ**.

QQQ is the neutral asset because the question is whether to add 3x Nasdaq
beta, hold the Nasdaq 1x, or step aside into T-bills. It is not a relative
value trade between QQQ and TQQQ.

## 2. Exact rules

All inputs use daily closes through session `t`. The target is set at the close
of `t` and executed at the first bar open of `t+1`. The shared 2% band applies.

Let `R_t = log(XLK_t) - log(XLU_t)`.

1. `m20_t = R_t - R_{t-20}` and `m60_t = R_t - R_{t-60}`.
2. `z20_t` is the z-score of `m20_t` against its trailing 252 observations
   (minimum 120); `z60_t` is the same for `m60_t`.
3. `score_t = (z20_t + z60_t) / 2`.
4. State:
   * **TQQQ** if `score_t >= +0.50`;
   * **BIL** if `score_t <= -0.50`;
   * **QQQ** otherwise.
5. During the z-score warm-up (score not finite), hold **QQQ**, never TQQQ.
6. Weights are long-only fractions of equity and sum to 1.

## 3. Data, decision clock, and causality

| Item | Choice |
|---|---|
| Signal | XLK and XLU adjusted daily closes from `data/external/` |
| Execution | local 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ/BIL panel via `research/bt.py` |
| Session calendar | QQQ regular sessions; external series reindexed/ffilled |
| Decision | close of session `t` (XLK/XLU close 16:00 ET, same session close) |
| Fill | first bar open of `t+1` |
| Costs | 1 bp headline, 5 bp and 10 bp reported |
| Band | 2% notional |
| Lag | none for XLK/XLU: their official close is stamped at the same 16:00 ET close used for the decision, and the fill is the next open |

The development run uses a panel that ends 2023-12-29. The external loader
reindexes to that panel's sessions, so no 2024-2026 price enters the signal or
the performance. A future-value perturbation audit replaces every XLK/XLU
value after the decision date with garbage and confirms that the target at
that date does not change.

## 4. Why this is not an existing family

* Not `ratio-froth` or `relative-value-tqqq`: there is no TQQQ/QQQ ratio, no
  ratio momentum, and no QQQ moving-average gate.
* Not `qqq-spy-relative`: that family ranks QQQ against SPY. Here the signal
  is a **sector** pair, XLK against XLU, and the position is TQQQ/BIL/QQQ.
* Not `family-beta-rotation`: beta is a covariance object. This family never
  estimates a covariance or an up/down beta; it uses the relative price path
  of two sectors.
* Not a volatility target, drawdown event, calendar clock, opening-range
  signal, or ML model. The XLK/XLU ratio is the primary object, not a filter
  layered on a QQQ price trend.
* The 252-session window is only a standardization lookback for the 20/60-day
  relative return; it is not a 100-250 day price-trend gate.
* The ratio is an external cross-sectional series; QQQ is only the traded
  asset and the neutral state.

## 5. Pre-registered 8-cell sensitivity grid

The grid is deliberately not a single 2 x 2 x 2: it includes the primary, three
threshold neighbours at the 20/60 blend, and the two single-horizon
alternatives at two settings. This exposes whether the blend or one horizon is
doing the work.

| Cell | Windows | TQQQ z | BIL z |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| **1 (primary)** | **20/60 blend** | **+0.50** | **-0.50** |
| 2 | 20/60 blend | +0.50 | -0.75 |
| 3 | 20/60 blend | +0.75 | -0.50 |
| 4 | 20/60 blend | +0.75 | -0.75 |
| 5 | 20 only | +0.50 | -0.50 |
| 6 | 20 only | +0.75 | -0.75 |
| 7 | 60 only | +0.50 | -0.50 |
| 8 | 60 only | +0.75 | -0.75 |

Fixed: 252-session z-window, 120 minimum observations, QQQ as the neutral
state, BIL as the defensive state. The primary is the centre of the mechanism,
not the best cell in the grid.

## 6. Falsifiers (pre-registered)

The family is killed if any of the following holds on the development window:

1. 1 bp CAGR <= 36.72% or 1 bp max DD >= 82.29% (the published TQQQ bar).
2. 10 bp CAGR <= 36.72% (the edge is a cost artefact).
3. The circular-shift placebo CAGR percentile is below 90%.
4. Daily-return correlation with any current family winner is above 0.95.
5. Fewer than 100 fills or fewer than 30 independent fill events.
6. Any of the three subperiods (2016-2019, 2020-2021, 2022-2023) has a
   negative CAGR.
7. A static book at the strategy's average weights matches the 1 bp CAGR
   within 1 percentage point (the timing adds nothing).
8. The future-value perturbation audit fails on any sampled date, or the
   close-to-next-open mapping audit fails (a causality bug).

The verdict is `dev_pass` only if all eight checks pass. A marginal 1 bp pass
with a 10 bp fail is still a fail: the family is not an above-TQQQ winner.

## 7. Expected effect

| metric | expectation |
|---|---|
| CAGR (1 bp) | 30-42% |
| max DD | 40-55% |
| Sharpe | 0.9-1.2 |
| average TQQQ weight | 0.25-0.35 |
| average QQQ weight | 0.40-0.55 |
| correlation to winners | 0.40-0.70 |

If the result is in these ranges with a positive placebo and a materially
worse static blend, the XLK/XLU object carries information. The main risks are
(a) the 20-day leg is noisy and generates turnover, (b) 2021-2022 sector
leadership whipsawed, and (c) the signal may partly proxy a QQQ momentum
switch. The report states these plainly.

code:
"""family-sector-rotation -- growth-vs-defensive sector leadership times TQQQ.

Primary object: the XLK/XLU relative return.  Tech leadership (XLK beating
XLU) is a broad risk-appetite signal, so the strategy holds TQQQ.  Defensive
leadership (XLU beating XLK) is a risk-off signal, so it holds BIL.  The
neutral middle holds QQQ.

The signal is the average of the 20-day and 60-day relative-return z-scores.
Each return is z-scored against its own trailing 252-session distribution, so
the 20-day and 60-day horizons are comparable and the state is not a raw price
trend gate.

Decision clock: a target is set from the close of session t (XLK/XLU closes
are 16:00 ET, the same session close) and executed at the next session's first
bar open.  Long only, weights sum to 1, 2% band.

Run ``python strategy.py`` from this directory to regenerate ``result.json``.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
import ext_harness as H

SLUG = "family-sector-rotation"
FAMILY = "sector-rotation"
PRIMARY = "XLK/XLU 20/60-day relative-return z-score"

END = H.END

PARAMS = {
    "windows": (20, 60),
    "z_window": 252,
    "min_periods": 120,
    "tqqq_z": 0.50,
    "bil_z": -0.50,
}

# 8-cell sensitivity grid: the primary, three threshold neighbours at the
# 20/60 blend, and the 20-only / 60-only alternatives at two settings.
PLATEAU = [
    {"windows": (20, 60), "tqqq_z": 0.50, "bil_z": -0.50},
    {"windows": (20, 60), "tqqq_z": 0.50, "bil_z": -0.75},
    {"windows": (20, 60), "tqqq_z": 0.75, "bil_z": -0.50},
    {"windows": (20, 60), "tqqq_z": 0.75, "bil_z": -0.75},
    {"windows": (20,), "tqqq_z": 0.50, "bil_z": -0.50},
    {"windows": (20,), "tqqq_z": 0.75, "bil_z": -0.75},
    {"windows": (60,), "tqqq_z": 0.50, "bil_z": -0.50},
    {"windows": (60,), "tqqq_z": 0.75, "bil_z": -0.75},
]


def _score(ext: pd.DataFrame, windows) -> pd.Series:
    rel = np.log(ext["XLK"]) - np.log(ext["XLU"])
    parts = [H.rolling_z(rel.diff(int(w)), PARAMS["z_window"],
                         PARAMS["min_periods"])
             for w in windows]
    return sum(parts) / len(parts)


def make_targets(ext: pd.DataFrame, params: dict | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    s = _score(ext, p["windows"])
    return H.state_weights(s, float(p["tqqq_z"]), float(p["bil_z"]))


def _limit(end):
    return pd.Timestamp(end) if end is not None else pd.Timestamp(END)


def _check_window(ts, limit) -> None:
    last = pd.Timestamp(ts[-1])
    if last.tzinfo is not None:
        last = last.tz_localize(None)
    if last.normalize() > limit:
        raise ValueError(
            "panel extends past the development window "
            f"{limit.date()}; 2024-2026 is not loaded")


def build_weights(ts, opens, closes, params: dict | None = None,
                  end=None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Minute weights; targets at session close t fill at t+1's open."""
    limit = _limit(end)
    _check_window(ts, limit)
    ext = H.aligned(ts, ["XLK", "XLU"], end=limit)
    return H.to_minutes(ts, make_targets(ext, params))


def main() -> None:
    ts, o, c = H.load_panel()
    ext = H.aligned(ts, ["XLK", "XLU"])
    targets = make_targets(ext)
    ev = H.evaluate(ts, o, c, targets, n_placebo=100)
    st = ev["stats"]["1bp"]
    kills = H.kill_checks(ev)
    plateau = H.plateau(ts, o, c,
                        lambda p: make_targets(ext, p), PLATEAU)
    causality = {
        "future_value_perturbation": H.perturb_audit(
            ext, make_targets, cutoff_offset=0),
        "close_to_next_open_mapping": H.mapping_audit(ts, targets),
    }
    ctrl_st, ctrl_ret = H.trend_control(ts, o, c, 0.50, -0.50)
    trend_control = {
        "name": "QQQ 20/60 momentum, same three-state map",
        "cagr": ctrl_st["cagr"],
        "max_drawdown": ctrl_st["max_drawdown"],
        "sharpe": ctrl_st["sharpe"],
        "corr_to_strategy": float(ev["_daily_ret"].corr(ctrl_ret)),
    }
    i = H.bt.start_index(ts, H.START)
    bench = H.bt.benchmark(c[i:, 1], ts[i:], H.BARS_PER_YEAR)
    payload = {
        "slug": SLUG,
        "family": FAMILY,
        "primary_object": PRIMARY,
        "dev": st,
        "windows": {"dev": {"1bp": ev["stats"]["1bp"],
                            "5bp": ev["stats"]["5bp"],
                            "10bp": ev["stats"]["10bp"]}},
        "window": {"dev": [H.START, H.END], "holdout": "not loaded"},
        "benchmark": {
            "tqqq_panel": bench,
            "tqqq_published_bar": H.TQQQ_BAR,
        },
        "params": {k: (list(v) if isinstance(v, tuple) else v)
                   for k, v in PARAMS.items()},
        "stats": ev["stats"],
        "events": ev["events"],
        "activity": {"fills": st["fills"], "events": ev["events"],
                     "fills_per_year": st["fills"] / st["years"],
                     "events_per_year": ev["events"] / st["years"]},
        "yearly": ev["yearly"],
        "subperiods": ev["subperiods"],
        "corr_winners": ev["corr_winners"],
        "corr_range": [min(ev["corr_winners"].values()),
                       max(ev["corr_winners"].values())],
        "avg_weights": ev["avg_weights"],
        "static_avg_weights": ev["static_avg_weights"],
        "plateau": plateau,
        "placebo": ev["placebo"],
        "causality_audit": causality,
        "trend_control": trend_control,
        "kill_checks": kills,
        "verdict": "dev_pass" if not any(kills.values()) else "fail",
        "timing": ("XLK/XLU daily closes through session t; target set at the "
                   "close of t, filled at the first bar open of t+1; 2% band; "
                   "long only."),
        "notes": ("XLK and XLU adjusted closes are read from data/external/ "
                  "and reindexed to the QQQ session calendar.  The development "
                  "run ends 2023-12-29 and does not load 2024-2026 prices."),
    }
    H.write_result(Path(__file__).with_name("result.json"), payload)
    print(f"{SLUG}: {H.summary_line(st)}")
    print("  10bp:", H.summary_line(ev["stats"]["10bp"]))
    print("  corr range", payload["corr_range"], "verdict", payload["verdict"])
    print("  kills", [k for k, v in kills.items() if v])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
